title: ephor out-of-process forge protocol
description: The protocol of FS-001-forge-interface.2: an executable named 'ephor-forge-<name>', resolved on PATH, invoked as 'ephor-forge-<name> <subcommand>' with a request as JSON on stdin and the answer as JSON on stdout. Diagnostics go to stderr; a non-zero exit is a failure, never an empty answer (FS-001-forge-interface.6). Subcommands: capabilities, pull-requests, issues, notices, messages, failures, restart, resolve-task, react, reply. An implementation answers the subcommands whose capabilities it declared; ephor never calls an undeclared one. This document defines the request shape and one response shape per subcommand; message, gate, and failure shapes are the answer envelope's $defs, referenced here so the two transports cannot drift (FS-001-forge-interface.2).

config.description: The provider block from the person's feed configuration, verbatim. Project keys, repository slugs, the user's address — the forge's business, opaque to ephor (FS-001-forge-interface.4).

project.description: The project the source is bound under (FS-001-forge-interface.9). Empty for a source bound once for the site, which is asked about no one project and whose answers ephor places, and for the capabilities probe.

user.description: The user's login on this forge, where ephor knows it. Omitted where it does not.

repo.description: failures and restart: the repository whose gate is being asked about.

number.description: failures and restart: the pull request whose gate is being asked about.

scope.description: restart only: how much of the gate to run again — only what is not green, or everything it covers. The caller's word, never the implementation's guess: the two are different asks and one of them spends an hour of a shared machine pool (FS-004-quick-actions.9).

tickets.description: issues only: the ticket keys to fetch, from registry branch inference.

target.description: resolve-task, react, and reply: the descriptor the implementation itself put on the message (task), on the message identity it reported (react), or on the thread (reply), handed back verbatim.

text.description: reply only: the message to send, as the person settled it — posted exactly as it stands (FS-005-dispatch.13).

emoji.description: react only: the reaction to post, as the emoji itself.

review.description: Embeds 'review' in the pull requests it returns: the user's own verdict on a change they were asked to look at (FS-001-forge-interface.1).

notices.description: Answers notices: the forge's own list of what it decided to tell the user (FS-001-forge-interface.1).

messages.description: Answers messages: the conversations addressed to the user in the other places people talk, each one whole (FS-001-forge-interface.1). An implementation that declares it should not also report the same conversations as notices: one id in both merges into one row, and the notice's verdict on whether it awaits the user would stand beside ephor's own.

reply_reconciliation.description: Opt-in durable repeat reconciliation (FS-001-forge-interface.1): look up the original operation before freshness checks, return its known remote acceptance without another delivery, and refuse changed payloads on a used descriptor. Queue admission is not acceptance.

capabilities_response.description: The capability set of FS-001-forge-interface.1. ephor degrades to what is declared; a probe that could not run is a failure, not an empty declaration (FS-001-forge-interface.6).

id.description: Stable within the forge, 'repo/number' by convention. ephor keys the matter as '<provider>:<id>' (FS-007-matters.1).

draft.description: Whether this pull request is still a draft. Omit it where the forge has no notion of drafts: absent is kept apart from `false`, because "not yet anybody's to review" is a claim about the world, and one nobody has made is not one made and answered no (FS-001-forge-interface.1). An unattended sweep reads it to decide whether a branch is somebody's to move (FS-004-quick-actions.6.1).

reasons.description: Every reason it is the user's (FS-001-forge-interface.1). Which side of the review that puts them on, and whether any of them means an answer is owed, is ephor's to decide (FS-001-forge-interface.3).

state.description: As the forge spells it; 'open:needs_work' and 'open:approved' refine open where reviewers have spoken.

cited.description: Whether the user is cited anywhere in the conversation — the forge knows its own mention syntax; whether the citation was answered is ephor's rule (FS-001-forge-interface.3).

review.description: The user's own review of this pull request, from an implementation declaring 'review' (FS-001-forge-interface.1). Omit it where they have not reviewed it; a verdict this vocabulary has no word for, such as an approval the forge dismissed, is no review.

threads.description: The conversation as ordered threads (FS-001-forge-interface.1). The channel is implicitly the pull request's review threads.

gate.description: Omitted entirely where the gate has no jobs and no verdict.

assignees.description: The logins holding this pull request, where the forge names them (FS-005-dispatch.31). Omit it where the forge does not report assignment: an omitted list and an empty one mean different things, and a selector asking about it refuses on the omission.

labels.description: The labels the forge carries on this pull request (FS-005-dispatch.31). Omit it where the forge has no notion of labels, for the reason 'assignees' is omitted.

reason.description: Why something is the user's, in the one vocabulary the protocol has (FS-001-forge-interface.1): they opened it, spoke in it, are named in it, were asked to review it, or have it assigned. A word outside it fails the whole answer.

reply.description: Present where this channel can carry a reply (FS-007-matters.4): the implementation's own descriptor for the thread, handed back to the reply subcommand verbatim. Absent means display-only, and a drafted answer is copy material (FS-005-dispatch.13).

thread.description: One thread of a conversation: its messages in order, and where a reply to it goes.

key.description: The ticket key as the tracker spells it ('GR-73955'). ephor keys the matter 'ticket:<key>'.

role.description: Whether the user opened this issue or merely takes part in it (FS-001-forge-interface.1). An implementation with no notion of the difference omits it, and everything it reports counts as the user's own.

assigned.description: Whether anyone has taken this issue, where the tracker holds that (FS-001-forge-interface.1). Omit it where the tracker has no notion of assignment: omitted and false mean different things, and what nobody claimed about is never counted as unclaimed work.

assignees.description: The logins holding this issue, where the tracker names them (FS-005-dispatch.31). 'assigned' says whether anybody has it; this says who. Omit it where the tracker does not report assignment: an omitted list and an empty one mean different things, and a selector asking about it refuses on the omission rather than reading it as unheld.

labels.description: The labels the tracker carries on this issue (FS-005-dispatch.31). Omit it where the tracker has no notion of labels, for the reason 'assignees' is omitted.

blocked_by.description: The tracker's own first-class dependencies for this issue (FS-001-forge-interface.1). Omit it where the tracker has no notion of dependencies; an empty list says it asked and there are none. An issue blocked by one still open awaits its prerequisite rather than its reader (FS-003-feed-categories.4).

messages.description: The comment tail, most recent last; bounded by the implementation.

status.description: As the tracker spells it; a finished status is what releases the dependent issue.

issue_dependency.description: One issue another is blocked by: who it is and where it stands, without its own conversation or dependencies.

id.description: Stable within the forge and across refreshes. ephor keys the row '<provider>:<repo>#<number>' where both are given and '<provider>:<id>' otherwise, and keeps the reader's unread state under it.

reason.description: The forge's own word for why it is telling the user: mention, team_mention, review_requested, assign, ci_activity, … Free-form: shown to the reader and matched against a few known words, so a reason ephor has never seen still arrives (FS-001-forge-interface.1).

subject.description: What the notice is about. 'other' is a release, an advisory, an invitation: still addressed to the reader, and the default.

repo.description: The repository the subject lives in, where the forge has that notion.

number.description: The subject's number within its repository: what makes this notice the same work as a pull request or issue another capability reported (FS-003-feed-categories.5).

read.description: The forge considers the user to have read it. Its own record, kept apart from ephor's unread tracking.

notices_response.description: Everything the forge says is directed at the user, whatever it is about. Answered exhaustively or not at all: a truncated list is a failure, never an answer (FS-001-forge-interface.6).

id.description: Stable across refreshes. ephor keys the row '<provider>:<id>' and keeps the reader's unread state under it. Read for nothing else: whatever it looks like, it is never taken for a repository or a number.

room.description: The room it is in, as the venue names it. Absent for a direct conversation.

reasons.description: Why it is the user's, in the vocabulary pull requests use.

threads.description: Its threads, each carrying its own reply descriptor. Each message says who wrote it and whether that was the user ('mine'); whether the conversation awaits the user, and what it refers to, are ephor's to work out from them, so a 'needs_response' sent here is ignored (FS-001-forge-interface.3).

conversation.description: One conversation addressed to the user in a place people talk that is not a forge (a chat room, a direct conversation, a mail thread), with its words (FS-001-forge-interface.1).

messages_response.description: The conversations addressed to the user. An implementation that cannot vouch that this is the venue as it is now fails rather than answering: an empty list is a quiet venue, never a listener that stopped hearing it (FS-001-forge-interface.6).

failures_response.description: What failed under the red gate of request.repo/request.number. The empty array is an answer — 'the gate is red and nothing failed', a gate blocked on approvals or unstarted jobs — and ephor then shows the blockers it already has. Asked on demand, never during refresh (FS-001-forge-interface.1).

asked.description: How many jobs the forge was asked to run again. Zero is an answer — nothing here needed restarting — and not a failure. Omit it where the forge takes the request and does not say how much it scheduled: that is an ordinary whole-gate start, and reporting it as zero would read as a restart that found nothing to do.

note.description: The forge's own sentence about what it did, shown verbatim. What answers the reader where 'asked' is omitted.

skipped.description: What could not be restarted, one line each: an external status somebody else's system wrote, a run too old to re-run. Reported rather than swallowed — a restart that silently did three quarters of the job is worse than one that says which quarter it skipped (FS-001-forge-interface.1).

restart_response.description: What the restart of request.repo/request.number actually asked for, at request.scope. A gate is minutes from saying anything itself, so this has to stand on its own until then (FS-004-quick-actions.9).

resolve_task_response.description: Empty object on success. A task already resolved is success: the state asked for is the state it is in.

reply_response.description: Both transports return known acceptance or explicitly unknown delivery (FS-001-forge-interface.2). Legacy empty-object success remains accepted; unknown is held for a checked resolution (FS-005-dispatch.13).
